rules.reason: fail at a branch forces it also in executions the natural cause never reaches, such as requests that succeeded; a chain continues through the boundary effects of the cause behind it.

Inside a library an outcome comes from what the library calls, and the same outcome injected at the library's own point can leave the library in a state the natural one never does: an error injected at pgxpool's Acquire disables inventory's single-connection pool, while the Acquire error an upstream fault causes returns at once. A chain continues through the business call site that receives the library's outcome.
As for a branch inside a library: a chain continues through the business call site that receives the error.
As for a branch inside a library: a chain continues through the business code that reads the answer.
Libraries get no delays, since their points are hot paths a delay at every execution would swamp.
More executions of a branch not taken only mean that more requests passed it.

An error of a type returned from a call is what fail raising that type substitutes there, such as the importable class at a Python call point. Without the type, fail raises what the call site's first handler names, which may take another path; where an SDK cannot know the type, nothing is known to correspond.
A Go call fail replaces the error at the err != nil check after the callee has run, so it fails work already done, which a natural error does not; a registered sentinel sits at the same check.
EOF at pq_getbyte is PostgreSQL noticing that its client closed the connection, a consequence of the client, whose own failure the chain reaches anyway.

A function of an upstream component returning its failure is what fail writing that failure returns, where the agent's configuration gives the value the function returns naturally: NULL from a read of Redis that finds no key, EOF from a PostgreSQL backend reading the end of its client's connection.
More successful calls only mean more executions.

negate flips every answer, also of executions the natural cause never touched, such as orders' retryable for reservations that succeeded; a chain continues through the boundary effects of the cause behind it.
An answer the detector already gave, given more often, may only mean more executions.
Extra iterations are read as contention, which a delay at the loop stands for.
A request never sent whole reached no peer, as when fail with a timeout keeps it from the peer.
The peer completed the request after the caller left, which fail_after reproduces: the call runs, then the caller sees a timeout.
The peer failed the request after the caller left and did not do its work, as when fail with a timeout keeps the request from the peer; fail_after would let the peer do it.
Without a response the peer wrote after the caller left, whether the peer did its work is unknown.
A refused connection is what fail with refused gives the caller.
A status answered to the caller is what fail with that exact status gives it; the caller acts on the exact code.
A status the server answered is what fail with that exact status answers.
A server answering after its caller left is the server noticing the caller's timeout, a consequence of the caller, whose own timeout the chain reaches anyway.
As for its count: a server answering after its caller left is a consequence of the caller.
More calls answered with success or a redirect only mean more executions.
More requests answered with success or a redirect only mean more executions.
A transport failure of no named kind has no action that names it.
A handler that raised has no action that names it.
A slower call is what a delay at the client stands for.
A slower handler is what a delay at the server stands for.
A read that found nothing is what empty returns.
A failed read is what fail returns.
More reads only mean more executions.
More rows per read is a change of the stored data that no store action produces.
More writes is what duplicate produces.
A failed write is what fail returns.
More rows per write is a change of the stored data that no store action produces.
A system call failing with EIO is what fail with EIO returns.
More system calls, or more would-block results of non-blocking sockets, only mean more work.
